public_rationale: On the plain reading, benchmark scores alone are a weak guide to broad, robust ability, and pre-post research supports that. Apple's ICLR 2025 GSM-Symbolic study found that every model tested lost accuracy when only the numbers in grade-school maths questions changed. Adding one irrelevant clause cut performance by up to 65%. 'The Leaderboard Illusion' (April 2025) found that Chatbot Arena gains reflected 'overfitting to Arena-specific dynamics rather than general model quality'. No source found shows benchmark success reliably tracking robust general capability. 'Limited' is a modest claim, and the evidence clears it.
limitations: The claim is partly conceptual. 'General intelligence' has no agreed measure, so the evidence shows benchmarks overstating robustness rather than measuring general intelligence directly.
The evidence covers specific benchmarks (GSM8K, Chatbot Arena), not all benchmarks.

our_interpretation: Plain reading: published evidence shows that high scores on AI benchmarks often do not carry over to robust performance when tasks change modestly, or reflect overfitting to the benchmark rather than general quality. So benchmark scores alone are a weak guide to general intelligence.
He describes an ongoing state with no period. Evaluator uses research published from 2024 up to the post date of 2026-02-17.
criteria.support_condition: Credible studies before the post show benchmark scores overstating general ability, for example performance drops under small perturbations, or leaderboard rankings reflecting overfitting rather than general quality.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Credible evidence that benchmark success reliably tracks robust general capability under novel conditions, with little gap between benchmark and perturbed or real-world performance.
